description: This line plot illustrates the Attack Success Rate (ASR) for three different trigger word insertion strategies—labeled “random,” “end,” and “brilliant”—across a series of trigger words on the SST-2 dataset with a clean-label poison rate of 5%. The y-axis represents ASR, scaled linearly from 0.2 to 0.9, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The x-axis lists the trigger words: “bb,” “mb,” “cf,” “beautiful,” “excellent,” “gorgeous,” “wonderful,” “brilliant,” “stunning,” and “beautifully.” The “random” strategy is depicted by an orange line with star markers and a solid line; it begins at an ASR of approximately 0.52, drops sharply to 0.2 near “cf,” then rises to nearly 0.9 before declining slightly. The “end” strategy is shown by a purple line with circle markers and a solid line; it starts at approximately 0.51, peaks at 0.85 near “gorgeous,” then declines to around 0.82 near “beautifully.” The “brilliant” strategy, represented by a teal line with triangle markers and a solid line, starts at 0.2, rises steadily to nearly 0.9 near “stunning,” and ends slightly above 0.88.
